title: Perps Pro scale order warns when a ladder would cross the book — Mobile
description: A trader building a scale (laddered) order on Perps Pro expects their rungs to rest on the book as passive orders. Any rung placed on the wrong side of the market fills instantly as a taker order instead, which defeats the point of laddering. This recipe proves the order form tells the trader when that is about to happen, distinguishes a partly-affected ladder from one that is entirely on the wrong side, re-evaluates the moment the trader edits an endpoint or flips their side, and never blocks them from placing the order anyway.

ensure-unlocked.intent: A returning trader gets back into their wallet

open-market.intent: The trader opens the {{params.market}} market they want to trade

wait-scale-fields.intent: The trader is looking at the laddered-order ticket, ready to choose a price range

go-long.intent: The trader starts from a clean slate, betting the market rises

set-orders.intent: The trader splits the ladder across two rungs

set-size.intent: The trader commits a size so the ticket is complete and placeable

safe-start.intent: The trader places the cheapest rung of their upward bet safely below the market

safe-end.intent: The trader keeps the far rung below the market too, so the whole ladder should rest

expect-quiet.intent: Nothing is wrong with this ladder, so the trader is left alone

partial-end.intent: The trader stretches only the far rung past the market, so part of the ladder would fill on the spot

expect-partial-above.text: Part of your price range is above current price
expect-partial-above.intent: The trader is told that only part of their order would fill immediately, not all of it

evidence-partial-scroll.intent: Bring the price range and the caution beneath it into plain sight

evidence-partial-shot.label: evidence-partial
evidence-partial-shot.intent: Show the trader being told only part of their ladder would fill at once

full-start.intent: The trader lifts the near rung above the market too, putting every rung on the wrong side

expect-full-above.text: Your price range is above current price
expect-full-above.intent: Now the whole order would fill immediately, and the wording escalates to say so

evidence-full-above-scroll.intent: Bring the price range and the caution beneath it into plain sight

evidence-full-above-shot.label: evidence-full-above
evidence-full-above-shot.intent: Show the trader being told their whole upward ladder would fill at once

flip-short.intent: The trader changes their mind and bets the market falls instead

expect-cleared-on-flip.intent: Those same prices are perfectly sensible for a downward bet, so the warning clears itself

short-start.intent: The trader sets the lower bound of the downward ladder under the market

short-end.intent: The trader keeps the upper bound under the market too, so every rung is on the wrong side

expect-full-below.text: Your price range is below current price
expect-full-below.intent: The trader gets the mirrored warning for a downward bet that would fill on the spot

evidence-full-below-scroll.intent: Bring the price range and the caution beneath it into plain sight

evidence-full-below-shot.label: evidence-full-below
evidence-full-below-shot.intent: Show the trader the mirrored caution for a downward ladder that would fill at once

expect-still-placeable.intent: The warning is advice, not a veto: the trader can still go ahead and place the order
